body.statement: For \(m\ge2\) and nonempty \(\mathcal C\), the common-response restriction \(R_{c,z}=R_c\) defines a strict submodel \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\subsetneq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sat}}\). For \(p^{\mathrm w}\) on arms \(\{1,2\}\), the response-type certificate \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm w}\) exhaustively enumerates \(|\mathcal R|=36\), \(|\mathcal R_{\mathrm F}|=144\) under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sat}}\), and \(72\) types under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\). Its feasible primal mixtures and valid endpoint inequalities certify \(\tau\in[-1/2,1]\) under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sat}}\) and \(\tau\in[0,1]\) under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\).
body.justification: The strict inclusion and witness separate saturated arm-specific off-target responses from the common-response submodel relevant to the fully excluded benchmark.
body.gap: Song et al. identify the larger all-exposure potential-outcome law under common excluded responses, whereas this proposition certifies that relaxing exclusion on \(\mathcal C\) can change bounds for a target-only contrast.
body.consumer: The witness is an exact regression test for response-type software and for the right-inverse implementation.
